rule: A pinned grammar is its wired bytes (sha256+length), its enumerable surface (id-order, type-set and field-set digests through web-tree-sitter, with the id/named/anonymous vocabularies recorded separately), the local copies those bytes are byte-identical to, the vendored source files (per-file sha256), and the authored provenance/decision record. Verification re-measures all of it and fails on ANY drift — including a vendored source edit, a vanished copy, or a name the vendored source declares that the wired wasm does not have. Regenerating the record is an explicit act (--write), never a silent side effect of verifying.

patches: P1 (grammar/statements/): `CONSTRAINT <name> UNIQUE | FOREIGN KEY | INDEX`. The only rule accepting a leading `CONSTRAINT <name>` accepted just `PRIMARY KEY` and `CHECK`, so the two most common named constraints in a real schema lost their names.

P3 (grammar/statements/): `grant_statement` / `revoke_statement` as VISIBLE nodes (upstream had the rules hidden, so the analyzer's GRANT/REVOKE arms named node types that no file could produce).

P4 (grammar/statements/do-drop-policy.js): `do_statement` and `drop_policy`. `keyword_do` existed but was wired only to MySQL's `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY DO UPDATE`; `keyword_policy` existed (create_policy needs it) but no drop rule used it.

FIX 3 (§3.3) `field`'s `optional($.directive)` becomes `optional($.directives)` — `{ f @a @b }` is the legal spelling of two directives on one selection
FIX 4 (§2.9.4) both string rules learn their escapes: the short string accepts `\` + any non-newline, the block string accepts `"""` and skips `\` as a unit

provenance.patchEvidence: Each FIX is one row of a 113-construct battery that names the specification section and states whether the construct is valid, so a failure can be classified as a GRAMMAR GAP (valid, rejected) or a CORRECT REJECTION (invalid, correctly rejected) rather than lumped together. Before/after on that battery: the previous wasm rejected 10 valid constructs, upstream `main` rejects 6, this build rejects 0, and all three reject the same 8 invalid constructs. The four FIXes were each confirmed to be necessary by building upstream and watching that construct fail there too. Artifacts: fixtures/graphql/out/grammar-gaps.json, fixtures/graphql/out/grammar-ab.json, fixtures/graphql/out/extraction-ab.json.

source.note: grammar.upstream.js (bkegley/tree-sitter-graphql@ee5ce96, VERBATIM — the fixed input, so the port is idempotent) + port.py (the patch AS CODE: the rename table and the four anchored FIX hunks, each refusing to write a half-ported grammar) + grammar.js (the GENERATED patched grammar, which is what `tree-sitter generate` reads) + tree-sitter.json (ABI 15) + package.json (deliberately no `"type"` field: the repo root is `"type": "module"` and grammar.js is CommonJS `module.exports`, so without a local package.json the tree-sitter CLI cannot load it) + LICENSE (MIT) + README.md (the divergence record, the regeneration sequence, and what the patch bought) + src/grammar.json + src/node-types.json. The two generated JSONs are vendored ON PURPOSE: `sourceVsWasmFor` needs the pair to run the offline source<->wasm proof, and without them the check reports `not applicable` and this lane has no such proof at all. src/parser.c IS vendored (284 KB), the same call hcl made at 600 KB and the opposite of nim at 41 MB: `measureVendored` hashes every file in the tree, tracked or not, so an untracked parser.c would turn the gate red after any `tree-sitter generate`. Tracking it makes the wired wasm rebuildable from TRACKED files alone and keeps the recorded digests still across a regeneration that changed nothing else. The exact three-command sequence is in README.md. A `node_modules` symlink points at the tree-sitter CLI during a build and is not tracked.

graphql.decision: Pin the local rebuild of the PATCHED vendored source. (1) The offline source<->wasm proof runs and is zero in both directions on the declared named types, re-measured by this gate on every run: every name the committed source declares exists in the wired wasm, and every wasm-named type is declared by the source. That is the offline statement that the committed bytes ARE a build of the committed source. (2) The wired build rejects 0 of 113 specification constructs, against 10 for the wasm it replaces and 6 for upstream `main`, while still correctly rejecting all 8 invalid constructs — so the patch is a strict improvement on BOTH the previous build and upstream, and does not trade correctness for permissiveness. (3) The extraction A/B over 47 real files, same analyzer both sides, moves 12 error files to 4, 20 error nodes to 7, and ADDS 4 symbols and 76 relationships; every single delta is enumerated and adjudicated in fixtures/graphql/REVIEW.md §E, and the direction is uniform. (4) The two most consequential upstream gaps (`interface I implements J`; a description on a `schema` block) both produced PUBLISHED PHANTOMS in the previous build, not merely missing facts, so this is a correctness pin and not a completeness one. (5) The PascalCase surface is preserved exactly, so no analyzer string literal, no stored symbol row and no m12/m14/m60 lane changes spelling — the one thing an upgrade must not do to this repository.

alternatives.option: pin the previous wasm as-is and document the two gaps as boundaries (what docs/analyzers/real-graphql-analyzer.md did)

A documented boundary is the right answer for a gap nobody can fix; a 12/47 error rate with phantom edges is not that.

alternatives.option: upgrade to bkegley/tree-sitter-graphql main (ee5ce96) unmodified
alternatives.measured: REJECTED on capability, and this is the load-bearing measurement of the lane: upstream names its rules snake_case (`object_type_definition`). The analyzer, the m12 shape-safety census, the m14 and m60 lanes and every stored symbol row assume `ObjectTypeDefinition`. Building upstream unmodified and running the node-type set difference gives 72 node types gained and 72 lost with identical names apart from casing — i.e. every construct routes through the analyzer's default arm and the file yields nothing. It also leaves 6 of its own gaps (ext-schema-multi, ext-schema-directives-only, ext-scalar, desc-block-escaped-triple, field-two-directives, apollo-link).

alternatives.option: hand-edit the vendored grammar.js in place, the way groovy's was hand-repaired

A hand edit leaves no record of what upstream did, is not re-derivable when upstream moves, and cannot be diffed as a patch. port.py keeps the upstream file verbatim, expresses the patch as four anchored hunks plus a rename table, refuses to write a half-ported grammar when an anchor is missing, and re-derives grammar.js byte-identically on every run. nim.decision: Pin the local rebuild, and the reason is a PROOF rather than a preference. (1) The vendored src/node-types.json declares exactly the named types the wired wasm materialises, and the wired wasm declares exactly the named types that source declares - zero in both directions, re-measured by this gate on every run. That is the offline statement that the committed bytes ARE a build of the committed source. (2) The wired build parses all 17 compiler-validated construct-matrix files with 0 ERROR and 0 MISSING, and every file in that matrix was first ACCEPTED by the real Nim 2.2.12 compiler (`nim check`), so a construct the compiler rejects could never be counted as evidence. (3) The grammar's own conformance suite passes 72/72 here. (4) The three other published tree-sitter-nim grammars were all cloned, generated and built, and each is rejected on a MEASURED ground: aMOPel cannot be loaded at all by the pinned runtime, haxscramper emits ZERO fields and 283 ERROR / 7 MISSING over the matrix because it transcribes the ABNF tokens of doc/grammar.txt as node types, and reo101 is a 9-line stub. (5) The external scanner makes a shared-parser lifecycle a live question rather than an assumption, so it was MEASURED: a fresh-parser-per-file reference against one shared parser over 47 files in two orders (file order, and a rotated order putting a different layout shape before each file) produced 0 differences in both, so the engine's cached-parser path is safe for nim and needs no lua-style isolation. Full table, the per-candidate numbers and the reproduction commands: grammars/tree-sitter-nim/PIN.md.

vb.decision: Pin as a local rebuild of a patched vendored source, and say plainly that this is the weakest pin in the file. There is no upstream release to pin: the repository publishes no npm package and no tagged release, and it is a 2-star project whose last push predates this lane. The wired bytes are therefore NOT byte-identical to anything published -- they are a build of a source this repo owns, and the pin's value is drift detection over THAT source (a hand edit to grammar.js moves the recorded digest and fails the gate) plus the source<->wasm proof that the committed bytes really are a build of the committed grammar. What the pin deliberately does NOT claim: that this is the best available VB.NET grammar. It is the best of the two that exist and the only one measured to parse real VB.NET at all (the alternative measured 29.50 % clean on the same draw), and it is NOT finished -- 90.89 % aggregate clean over 1185 files with 0 crash files, so roughly one file in eleven still carries an ERROR. The gate's floor is the number that has to move, and the long-tail defect census (fixtures/probes/defect-census.ts) is the work list that has to shrink it.

patches: REPAIR 1 (scanner, `common/scanner.h` `scan_pi_content`): the trailing `advance_if_eq(lexer, '\n')` became `skip_if_eq`. `advance_if_eq` is defined as `if (!eof && lookahead==chr) advance(lexer); else return false`, so its `else` ABORTS the caller — and the caller had already committed, past `mark_end`, on a lookahead whose value is irrelevant. A processing instruction with content therefore produced no `_pi_content` token, `<?target content?>` could not complete, and the parser wrapped the whole `<?...?>` in an ERROR node. It was not merely a lost declaration: with no XMLDecl present the enclosing `prolog` node disappeared too, taking any DOCTYPE in the same prolog with it. A 19-shape battery isolates it exactly: the construct parses iff the byte after `?>` is `\n` (fixtures/xml/out/pi-rootcause.json). `check_word` and `scan_comment` keep `advance_if_eq`, where a mismatch correctly means "not the token I was asked for".

REPAIR 2 (grammar, `xml/grammar.js` `_intSubset`): the internal subset is now `repeat(choice($._markupdecl, $.conditionalSect, $._DeclSep))` over a named `_intSubsetItem` rule, and `conditionalSect` is declared. Upstream could not reach a conditional section from an internal subset at ANY version measured: 0.5.0-0.6.x declare `conditionalSect` in the `dtd` grammar and inline it, but `_intSubset` referenced `$._markupdecl`, which does not include it; 0.7.0, which the wired wasm matches exactly, does not declare it in the `xml` grammar at all. The failure was destructive, not silent: `<![INCLUDE[...]]>` wrapped the `doctypedecl` in an ERROR and the parser then took a LATER `Name` as the DTD's name, so the analyzer published a Type symbol literally named `INCLUDE`. The named `_intSubsetItem` is because tree-sitter rejects a rule that can match the empty string and XML 1.0 permits an empty internal subset; writing the repeat at each use site keeps the generated `node-types.json` free of a wrapper node.

xml.decision: Pin the local rebuild of the PATCHED vendored source, and record that the pre-repair bytes needed no provenance work at all. (1) The pre-repair wired wasm is an UNMODIFIED upstream build: its enumerable surface is byte-for-byte the surface of a build of upstream HEAD 0.7.0 (140 node types, 2 fields, zero set difference in either direction) and its behaviour matches that build on all 29 constructs of the A/B battery. So unlike Groovy this was not a stale blob; it was current upstream, and the two defects are UPSTREAM defects that upstream's own test corpus never exercises — `grep -rn 'PITarget' test/corpus/` returns nothing, and the only `PI`-adjacent tests are `StyleSheetPI`/`XmlModelPI`. (2) Because the defects are upstream's, no upgrade fixes them: v0.5.0, v0.6.4 and v0.7.0 all fail both, which is the measurement that makes the repair necessary rather than optional. (3) Upgrading past 0.7.0 would DELETE capability, not add it: 0.7.0 already split DTD into a separate `dtd` grammar, and adopting a split would strand `elementdecl`, `AttlistDecl`, `AttDef`, `GEDecl`, `PEDecl` and `NotationDecl` — the analyzer's entire DTD surface — in a grammar this engine does not wire. (4) The repair is admissible on the corpus A/B above: 31 files repaired against 2 adjudicated out-of-surface/negative-control movements, and corpus MISSING nodes down 32 -> 10. (5) The offline source<->wasm proof runs and is measured on every gate run.

alternatives.option: pin the pre-repair bytes as-is and document the two defects as boundaries (what docs/analyzers/real-xml-analyzer.md does today)
alternatives.measured: REJECTED on capability, and the cost is the whole declaration vocabulary of a DTD. A content-bearing processing instruction is one of the most common constructs in XML, and it does not merely lose a symbol: with no XMLDecl present the enclosing `prolog` node is destroyed, so `<!DOCTYPE …>` in the same prolog is lost with it, and in a conditional section the parser picks a later `Name` as the DTD name and the analyzer publishes a Type symbol called `INCLUDE`. A documented boundary is right for a gap nobody can fix; this one is fixable in two lines and the fix is measured.

alternatives.option: upgrade to upstream HEAD 0.7.0 unmodified
alternatives.measured: REJECTED, and this is the negative result worth keeping: the pre-repair wired bytes ALREADY ARE 0.7.0. Surface-identical (140 types, 2 fields, zero difference either way) and behaviourally identical on all 29 battery constructs, so the upgrade buys nothing — and it leaves both defects in place, because they are upstream's. Separately, 0.7.0's split of DTD into its own `dtd` grammar means the `xml` grammar alone cannot represent a standalone `.dtd` file at all (root node type ERROR, measured), which is filed as a separate finding rather than solved by a swap.

alternatives.option: hand-edit the vendored grammar in place, the way groovy's was hand-repaired
alternatives.measured: REJECTED on re-derivability, and it matters more here than for Groovy. Both repairs are in files a future `tree-sitter generate` or upstream sync would otherwise be diffed against, and REPAIR 2 changes a GRAMMAR RULE (so `src/parser.c` is regenerated) while REPAIR 1 changes a SCANNER HEADER (so it is not). A hand edit leaves no record of which is which; the patch list above, the PIN.md record and the per-file digests below make the divergence from 0.7.0 auditable in one read, and `common/scanner.h` is 155 lines of upstream source so the delta is three added lines and one changed line.

alternatives.option: wire upstream's separate `dtd` grammar as a second language for `.dtd`
alternatives.measured: NOT TAKEN, and recorded as owed rather than rejected. It is measurably the right grammar — it parses libxml2's `cond_sect1.dtd` and `cond_sect2.dtd`, which the `xml` grammar cannot represent at all (root ERROR, 11 and 8 ERROR nodes), with 0 ERROR nodes — but it is a new wired language, a new router entry, a new analyzer and a new lane, not a repair. The measurement is kept so the decision is revisit-able with numbers instead of a recollection.
